pinyin: qián shì bù wàng, hòu shì zhī shī
gloss: Remember the past to guide the future.
teaser: Today, we explore how our past experiences shape our future decisions.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we explore how our past experiences shape our future decisions. [break 1s] The phrase is: 前事不忘，后事之师, qián shì bù wàng, hòu shì zhī shī. [break 1s] 前 (qián) - before [break 0.5s] 事 (shì) - matter/event [break 0.5s] 不 (bù) - not [break 0.5s] 忘 (wàng) - forget [break 0.5s] ， [break 0.5s] 后 (hòu) - after [break 0.5s] 事 (shì) - matter/event [break 0.5s] 之 (zhī) - of [break 0.5s] 师 (shī) - teacher/guide. [break 1s] So the full idiom, 前事不忘，后事之师, translates literally to 'Those who do not forget the past will find the future a teacher.' Figuratively, it means 'Remember the past to guide the future.' [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom emphasizes the importance of learning from past experiences. It originates from the idea that history serves as a valuable teacher. By reflecting on previous events, we can avoid making the same mistakes. Many renowned leaders and thinkers have echoed this wisdom throughout history. [break 1.5s] Example one: 我们应该记住前事不忘，后事之师。 [break 1s] We should remember that past events guide our future. [break 1s] Example two: 她总是从错误中学习，前事不忘，后事之师。 [break 1s] She always learns from her mistakes; remembering the past guides her future. [break 1s] Example three: 这本书教导我们前事不忘，后事之师的重要性。 [break 1s] This book teaches us the importance of remembering the past to guide the future. [break 1s] So, remember, 前事不忘，后事之师 means 'Remember the past to guide the future.' Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
